learningSteps.sourceQuote: **Factory supplies the machinery; SHIELD supplies the operating model.**
learningSteps.purpose: Separate the execution host from the portable delivery rules.
learningSteps.question: What does Factory provide, and what must remain owned by SHIELD?
learningSteps.explanation: Factory supplies sessions, Droids, tools, parallel execution, and host context. SHIELD owns the portable meaning of seats, scope, effects, reviews, evidence, and delivery.
learningSteps.whyItMatters: This prevents SHIELD from wrapping Factory while keeping the workflow portable to another host.

learningSteps.sourceQuote:
same product meaning should survive when Factory, Codex, Copilot, or a local
model executes the work, even though each host has different capabilities and
adapters.
learningSteps.purpose: Distinguish portable semantics from identical host behavior.
learningSteps.question: What should remain the same when the AI host changes?
learningSteps.explanation: The task, seat, authority, evidence, and delivery contracts remain stable. Tool availability and execution mechanics may differ and must be recorded honestly.
learningSteps.whyItMatters: Portability should preserve meaning without pretending every host has the same powers.

title: What gets installed in a repository

learningSteps.sourceQuote: SHIELD arrives as ordinary repository content in layers:
learningSteps.purpose: See installation as a small stack of repository-owned contracts and adapters.
learningSteps.question: What are the four layers, and which layer turns instructions into executable rails?
learningSteps.explanation: Seat instructions define responsibilities, host adapters connect the runtime, machine contracts bind packets, and the rail packages enforce transitions and effects in software.
learningSteps.whyItMatters: The layers let SHIELD start as understandable repository guidance and become deterministic without belonging to one vendor.

learningSteps.sourceQuote: The installation is therefore closer to Git than to one AI chat
learningSteps.purpose: Understand where the durable operating model lives.
learningSteps.question: Why is the Git comparison useful, and where might it be misleading?
learningSteps.explanation: The configuration and contracts travel with the repository instead of one conversation. Unlike Git, SHIELD still needs host adapters and installed packages before every behavior is enforceable.
learningSteps.whyItMatters: This is the promise you can make to another team without overstating today's installation experience.

learningSteps.sourceQuote: The persistent parent Factory chat occupies the **Hill seat**.
learningSteps.purpose: Keep role identity separate from runtime identity.
learningSteps.question: What changes when a different model occupies Hill, and what must not change?
learningSteps.explanation: The executor and model identity change. Hill's scope, sequencing, exception, and bookkeeping responsibilities remain the same and are recorded separately.
learningSteps.whyItMatters: A seat-first design keeps governance recognizable while models and products evolve.

learningSteps.sourceQuote:
Hill does not implement, review its
own plan, validate its own work, or simulate a human decision.
learningSteps.purpose: Prevent the persistent coordinator from absorbing every responsibility.
learningSteps.question: Which responsibilities stay outside Hill even when this parent chat has the broadest context?
learningSteps.explanation: May implements, Fury independently reviews, Mack validates, and humans make consequential human decisions. Hill keeps the work moving and routes exceptions.
learningSteps.whyItMatters: Broad context is useful only when independent checks remain independent.

title: Fresh specialists and meaningful human gates

learningSteps.sourceQuote: Hill dispatches fresh-context specialist Droids with bounded packets:
learningSteps.purpose: Understand how specialists receive enough context without inheriting the whole conversation.
learningSteps.question: What must a specialist packet contain so Daisy, Fury, May, or Mack can work independently?
learningSteps.explanation: The packet carries the exact objective, revision, paths, effects, evidence, validation, and handoff appropriate to that seat.
learningSteps.whyItMatters: Bounded packets make fresh context an advantage instead of a source of rediscovery.

learningSteps.sourceQuote:
Coulson, Fitz, and Simmons remain human seats and are never spawned or
simulated.
learningSteps.purpose: Locate real human authority without turning every transition into a gate.
learningSteps.question: What should reach a human, and what should continue automatically?
learningSteps.explanation: Consequential authority, acceptance, and excluded effects reach the accountable person. Routine in-envelope mechanics and correctable failures advance through software and bounded agent judgment.
learningSteps.whyItMatters: The human remains in control without becoming the team's packet courier.

title: How one Track-Layer construction run moves

learningSteps.sourceQuote:
Epic Wheels Up records one human GO for the accepted construction graph and
   envelope.
learningSteps.purpose: Understand what one program-level GO authorizes.
learningSteps.question: What can proceed after Epic Wheels Up, and which changes still require amendment?
learningSteps.explanation: Accepted features and bounded corrections may continue through draft publication. Changes to the promised outcome, graph, paths, milestones, host or autonomy, budget, material risk, or effect envelope require a recorded amendment.
learningSteps.whyItMatters: One meaningful GO creates autonomy without becoming unlimited authority.

learningSteps.sourceQuote: Epic Wheels Up is the Track-Layer construction pattern.
learningSteps.purpose: Avoid applying construction-program authority to ordinary product delivery.
learningSteps.question: Why must Track-Layer and ordinary delivery remain distinct?
learningSteps.explanation: Track-Layer builds a frozen architecture graph under one program envelope. Ordinary delivery follows a lighter issue rail and receives only the authority appropriate to that issue.
learningSteps.whyItMatters: The distinction keeps the fast construction pattern from silently broadening everyday authority.

learningSteps.sourceQuote:
Today, the architecture, manifest, repository seat instructions, and legacy
SHIELD implementation are real.
learningSteps.purpose: Separate current evidence from planned construction outputs.
learningSteps.question: Which SHIELD-inside-Factory pieces can be demonstrated now, and which begin with MR-000?
learningSteps.explanation: The architecture, manifest, seat guidance, and legacy implementation exist now. Factory Droids, the packet verifier, new quality targets, and Mission Rail packages are still construction work.
learningSteps.whyItMatters: An honest boundary makes the roadmap credible and prevents a written contract from being demonstrated as finished software.

learningSteps.sourceQuote:
The rebuild moves enforcement from agent memory into
small, testable software contracts.
learningSteps.purpose: Name the concrete outcome of the rebuild.
learningSteps.question: What changes when SHIELD moves from contract-by-instruction to contract-by-machine?
learningSteps.explanation: Agents no longer have to remember or hand-compose the next legal operation. Small libraries derive, validate, record, and project the workflow deterministically.
learningSteps.whyItMatters: This is the difference between a promising team convention and a reusable product rail.
